description: Find AINSOF music from a written brief — mood, scene, genre, energy, instruments. Example: 'lo-fi hip hop underscore, warm, no vocals'. Send the user's original language and musical intent, including durations and exclusions. Each call is self-contained. For a refinement, combine the current musical requirements and the latest change into brief; do not send only the clarification question. Send only musical requirements, never chat transcripts, assistant replies or unrelated personal information. Pass the customer's musical request in their original language, preserving their words, exclusions and durations. Do not add instruments, genres, mood, energy or vocal restrictions that they did not ask for. For a refinement, combine only the customer's established requirements and latest change, not suggestions from an assistant. One search returns evaluated matches or alternatives; present that result before proposing another direction. An unavailable search is a technical failure, not an empty catalogue: explain it and do not automatically repeat or broaden the request. A user-requested retry remains possible. Use the returned understanding, followups and selected preview version when presenting the answer. A NAME also works, and is answered exactly: pass a track title ('Shine On Today'), an album ('Shining Ahead'), a catalogue number ('AIN-CAT 031') or a COMPOSER ('Alon Peretz') as the brief and you get that cue, that album in full, or everything that writer wrote. A composer named inside an ordinary brief puts their cues first without narrowing it. NEVER tell a user we do not have a track until you have passed its name here.

brief.description: What the music should be — or the exact name of a track, album or catalogue number.

scope.description: Optional library restriction; omit to let the request select the library.

name: search_music
